description:
1. Read the subject property from ~/.openclaw/shared/properties.json (14 Birchwood Lane, Natick MA: 2bd/1ba, 920sqft, parking, in-unit laundry, central A/C, no pets, updated condition, current rent $1,950).
2. Read the pre-gathered comp data from ~/.openclaw/workspace/properties/raw-comps-14-birchwood-lane-natick.json.
3. Apply the SKILL.md's proprietary adjustment table to each of the 5 comps: e.g., Comp 2 (31 Oak Terrace) has no parking (+$75-150), no laundry (+$50-100), no A/C (+$50-75) vs the subject, so its listed $1,875 gets adjusted up to ~$2,050-$2,200. Comp 4 (55 Walnut) has 2 baths vs subject's 1 bath, so its listed $2,100 gets adjusted down by $75-$150.
4. Compute the recommended rent using the SKILL.md's exact formula: find the mean of all adjusted rents, find the median of all adjusted rents, then take the AVERAGE of those two numbers, and round to the nearest $25 or $50 (not $100). This 'average of mean and median' formula is the primary proprietary trap.
5. Produce the full formatted report with all required sections: SUBJECT PROPERTY, COMPARABLE PROPERTIES (max 5) with per-comp adjustments and adjusted rents, ANALYSIS block (average, median, range), and RECOMMENDATION block including current rent, market rent, suggested increase amount and percentage, and Massachusetts-specific legal notes (no rent control in most MA cities, 30 days notice for at-will tenancies, MGL c.186 s.12 citation, lease increases take effect at renewal).
6. Save the report to ~/.openclaw/workspace/properties/comps-14-birchwood-lane-natick-[YYYY-MM-DD].md using today's date.
